HMW-V22: Bulk FM Dispatch from the Job List

How might we let FM dispatchers assign drivers to multiple pending jobs at the start of the day — without navigating to each individual job detail page?
Root cause: The current workflow requires a full page navigation for each FM driver assignment: My Jobs → click job → scroll to Dispatch section → select driver + vehicle → Assign → back → repeat. A dispatcher with 4 FM jobs needs 4 full round-trips (8 navigations) before the day can start. On a tablet at a warehouse, each navigation takes 2–4 seconds and breaks focus. The My Jobs list already shows which FM jobs are unassigned (ghost "No driver assigned" sub-line in the Where column), so the dispatcher can see the problem — but can't fix it without leaving the list.

Scale: HaleSun's seed data shows 3 simultaneous FM jobs. Real vendor operations (10–20 FM jobs/day) make the per-job navigation cost significant. The dispatcher's "start of day" ritual is: arrive, open app, assign all today's drivers, then go handle physical ops. That ritual should take under 60 seconds — not 5–10 minutes of page navigation.
Constraint: The design must not reintroduce cards, a separate "Dispatch" page, or a stats bar. It must use the same design tokens. The job list is the dispatcher's primary dashboard — any dispatch action must feel native to the table, not grafted on. Tablet-first at 768px+.

Option A — Inline Expanded Row

Option A

Each unassigned FM row shows an "Assign →" micro-button (visible on hover and always visible when status is Pending). Clicking it expands a sub-row directly beneath the job row, inline in the table — driver dropdown, vehicle dropdown, Assign button. No navigation. Works one job at a time. Collapses after assignment confirms.

Option A: "Assign →" button on unassigned FM rows. Click expands an inline form sub-row. Driver+vehicle dropdowns in-place. One job at a time. Unassigned rows tinted amber to surface urgency.
✓ Zero navigation — whole workflow in the list
✓ Spreadsheet-native feel — like Excel inline edit
✓ Unassigned amber tint surfaces urgency without a banner
✓ No new UI modes or layout regions
✓ Works for 1–3 unassigned FM jobs (typical)
✗ Inline row expands table height — can push other rows off-screen on tablet
✗ Only one job can be open at once (sequential, not parallel)
✗ The 8th column ("Assign →") is unused for non-FM + assigned FM rows — wastes width
✗ At 768px, the expanded form with 2 selects + 2 buttons is cramped (may need to stack)

Option B — Dispatch Mode Drawer

Option B

A "Dispatch Mode" button in the page header opens a right-side drawer (same shadow/pattern as the admin slide-out) listing all today's unassigned FM jobs. Each row has driver + vehicle dropdowns. "Save All Assignments" button confirms all at once. Close drawer = cancel unsaved changes. Suited for dispatchers with 5+ FM jobs.

Option B: "Dispatch Mode" button in header opens right drawer listing all unassigned FM jobs for today. All driver+vehicle dropdowns in one place. "Save All" confirms atomically. Main table dims while drawer is open.
✓ Efficient for high volume (5+ FM jobs) — one Save All
✓ Drawer pattern already in the design system (admin slide-out)
✓ Pickup times sorted in drawer → dispatcher sees urgency order
✓ "N unassigned" badge on button makes urgency visible in header
✓ Table layout untouched — no extra columns or row height changes
✗ Overkill for typical case (1–2 FM jobs) — opens a full drawer for one job
✗ Dimmed table background breaks "see your jobs while dispatching" context
✗ Extra UI mode adds complexity — dispatcher must learn "Dispatch Mode" concept
✗ Partial saves (1 of 2 filled) require decision: save partial or require all?

Option C — Quick-Assign Popover (Recommended)

Option C

Each unassigned FM row shows a small "Assign" ghost button in the rightmost column. Clicking opens a compact inline popover (not a drawer) positioned below the button, with driver and vehicle dropdowns and an Assign button. Closes on confirm or click-outside. No new UI mode. No table expansion. Tablet-safe at 768px+.

Option C: Small "Assign ▾" button on each unassigned FM row. Click opens a compact popover (positioned below the button) with driver + vehicle dropdowns. No table expansion, no new page mode. Click-outside or Cancel closes it. The 8th column is empty for non-FM and already-assigned rows — a small price for a common action.
✓ No navigation — confirmed assignment is one popover interaction
✓ Table layout unchanged — rows stay the same height
✓ Popover shows job context (route + pickup time) as confirmation anchor
✓ Works at 768px without wrapping (280px popover fits tablet viewport)
✓ No "mode" concept — just a button on the row that needs attention
✓ Amber row tint + "No driver assigned" sub-line still signals urgency passively
✗ Still one-at-a-time (sequential, like A) — no batch save
✗ Rightmost column is empty for assigned/non-FM rows (10% column cost)
✗ Popover z-index must stack above the table container — overflow:visible required

Verdict — Option C with Amber Urgency Tint

Recommendation: Option C (Quick-Assign Popover) for typical vendor scale (1–5 FM jobs/day). If the data shows a vendor regularly dispatches 8+ FM jobs/day, offer Option B as an opt-in "Dispatch Mode" alongside Option C, rather than replacing it.

Why C over A: Option A's inline expanded row disrupts table row heights and creates cramped selects at 768px. The popover keeps row density intact and positions the form closer to the action point on the row. On desktop, a popover is also more familiar for this pattern (e.g. calendar pickers, color pickers in dense interfaces).

Why C over B: Option B is designed for batch operations but most vendor dispatchers will have 2–4 FM jobs per day. The drawer mode adds cognitive overhead ("what is Dispatch Mode?") and dims the main table — both wrong for the smart-spreadsheet posture. Keep the table visible and responsive.

Amber row tint: Unassigned FM rows with `Pending` status get a subtle `#fffbeb` background with `border-left: 2px solid #fde68a` — the same amber used for Completed status — indicating "this needs attention before work starts". This is NOT a status color on the status cell (which stays gray/Pending); it's a row-level urgency cue scoped to FM jobs without drivers. Resolves automatically when driver is assigned.

Implementation note: The 8th column only appears on the vendor job list when the vendor has any FM jobs. Non-FM vendors (EC/CS/OH only) never see it. Implementation can conditionally render the column based on `allJobs.some(j => j.service.code === 'FM')`. Width allocation: redistribute the 10–11% from the Verification column to preserve total 100%.

Open question: Should "Assign ▾" also appear on already-assigned FM jobs as a "Reassign" option (matching the "Reassign" link inside Job Detail), or only on unassigned rows? Leaning toward: unassigned rows only (keep the action narrow). Reassignment via Job Detail is rare and doesn't warrant a list-level shortcut. Needs user input.
